question.problem: Given the curve  $r(t)=⟨2{e}^{t},\,3{e}^{t},\,6{e}^{t}⟩,$ $t\ge 0,$ for which the arc length $s$ from $r(0)$ to $r(t)$ is given by $s=7({e}^{t}-1),$ find the corresponding unit tangent $T(s),$ parametrized by $s.$

current_example.problem: Given the curve  $\mathbf r(t)=\cos{t}\,\mathbf i - \sin{t}\,\mathbf j+\sqrt{3}t\,\mathbf k, \, t \geq 0,$ for which the arc length $s$ from $\mathbf r(0)$ to $\mathbf r(t)$ is given by $s=2t,$ find the corresponding unit tangent $\mathbf{T}(s),$ parametrized by $s.$
current_example.worked_solution:
First, since $s=2t,$ we have that $t=\dfrac{s}{2}.$

Therefore, the vector function $\mathbf R(s)$ that parametrizes $\mathbf r(t)$ by its arc length is

$$
\begin{aligned}R(s) & =r(\frac{s}{2}) \\  & =\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{s}{2})\,i-\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{s}{2})\,j+\sqrt{3}\cdot \frac{s}{2}k \\  & =\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{s}{2})\,i-\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{s}{2})\,j+\frac{\sqrt{3}s}{2}\,k.\end{aligned}
$$

 

Now, since the curve is parametrized by its arc length $s,$ the unit tangent can be found as

$$
\mathbf T(s) = \dfrac{\textrm{d}}{\textrm{d}s}\mathbf R(s).
$$

So, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}T(s) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}R(s) \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{s}{2}))\,i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(-\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{s}{2}))j+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(\frac{\sqrt{3}s}{2})k \\  & =-\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{s}{2})\,i-\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{s}{2})\,j+\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\,k \\  & =\frac{1}{2}(-\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{s}{2})\,i-\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{s}{2})\,j+\sqrt{3}\,k).\end{aligned}
$$
